question: How many paintings from the Rijksmuseum are in the collection?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:museum "rijksmuseum" ; mc:dataset "paintings-1850-1900" . }
explanation: This counts the Rijksmuseum works in the 1850–1900 paintings collection, which is what an unqualified question about "paintings" refers to here. It leaves out the Rijksmuseum's Rembrandt works, which are a separate collection in this graph.

question: How many paintings by Claude Monet are there?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p . ?p rdfs:label "Claude Monet" }
explanation: This counts the works plainly attributed to Claude Monet. His works here come from the 1850–1900 paintings collection (Rijksmuseum, The Met and the Art Institute of Chicago), so paintings he made outside those years are not included. Works only 'after' or 'attributed to' Monet are left out.

question: Which Vincent van Gogh paintings does the Met have?
sparql: SELECT ?w ?title WHERE { ?w mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum "met" ; dcterms:title ?title . ?p rdfs:label "Vincent van Gogh" }
explanation: Lists works at The Met that are plainly by Vincent van Gogh (matched by his exact name). Works only attributed to him, or made after or in imitation of him, are left out.

question: Which artists have paintings in all three museums?
explanation: This lists artists who plainly made at least one painting in each of the three museums of the 1850–1900 paintings collection: the Rijksmuseum, The Met and the Art Institute of Chicago. Works only 'attributed to' or 'after' an artist are not counted.

question: How many artists have works in more than one museum?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(?p) AS ?artists) WHERE { { SELECT ?p WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:artist ?p ; mc:museum ?m . } GROUP BY ?p HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?m) > 1) } }
explanation: This counts the people credited directly as the artist (`mc:artist`) on works held by at least two different museums. It covers both collections and leaves out 'after', 'attributed to' and 'workshop of' attributions.

question: Show me landscapes at the Rijksmuseum.
explanation: This lists Rijksmuseum works whose subject is a landscape-type concept, including subjects suggested by AI. It covers both collections (1850–1900 paintings and Rembrandt's works), so Rembrandt's landscape prints and drawings appear too.

question: Which Impressionist paintings show snow?
explanation: Looks for works in the 1850–1900 paintings collection whose museum-stated or Wikidata-inferred style is Impressionism and that have a 'snow' subject. The subjects include AI-suggested ones as well as those the museums recorded.

question: How many paintings have subjects that were suggested by AI rather than recorded by the museum?
explanation: This counts paintings in the 1850–1900 collection that have at least one AI-suggested subject (confidence of 0.6 or higher) which the museum did not also record for that painting.

question: Which paintings did the AI tag with night that the museum didn't?
explanation: This lists paintings from the 1850–1900 collection where the AI suggested the subject "night" but the museum's own subjects don't include a concept labelled "night". Only AI suggestions with confidence of at least 0.6 count, because only those are linked to works as subjects.

question: When was Berthe Morisot born and when did she die?
sparql: SELECT ?p ?birthYear ?deathYear WHERE { ?p rdfs:label "Berthe Morisot" . OPTIONAL { ?p mc:birthYear ?birthYear } OPTIONAL { ?p mc:deathYear ?deathYear } }
explanation: This looks up the person labelled exactly "Berthe Morisot" and returns her birth and death years as the graph records them, which are years only, not full dates.

question: Which artists in the collection belong to the Hague School?
explanation: Lists the artists of works in the collection whose movement on Wikidata is the Hague School. It only counts artists whose works are plainly by them, not works merely 'after' or 'attributed to' them.

question: How many paintings were begun in the 1880s?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:dataset "paintings-1850-1900" ; mc:beginYear ?y . FILTER(?y >= 1880 && ?y <= 1889) }
explanation: Counts works in the 1850–1900 paintings collection whose begin year falls between 1880 and 1889. The question names no artist, so the Rembrandt collection is left out.

question: How many paintings does each museum have?
sparql: SELECT ?museum (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:dataset "paintings-1850-1900" ; mc:museum ?museum . } GROUP BY ?museum ORDER BY DESC(?n)
explanation: This counts the works in the 1850–1900 paintings collection (Rijksmuseum, The Met and the Art Institute of Chicago), grouped by museum. Because the question names no artist, it leaves out the separate Rembrandt collection.

question: Which five artists have the most paintings?
explanation: This counts paintings in the 1850–1900 paintings collection (Rijksmuseum, The Met and the Art Institute of Chicago) for each artist and returns the five with the most. Only works plainly by the artist count, not ones merely 'after' or 'attributed to' them.

question: Find paintings of boats from before 1870.
explanation: Looks in the 1850–1900 paintings collection for works begun before 1870 whose subjects include "boat" or "boats". This covers both subjects the museums recorded and AI-suggested subjects.

question: How many artist records were matched by a person approving an AI suggestion?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?a) AS ?records) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?p) AS ?people) WHERE { ?p mc:sourceAgent ?a . ?a mc:matchMethod "human-approved" }
explanation: This counts the museum artist records whose match method is "human-approved", and also how many distinct people they belong to. The graph records that a person approved these matches, but it does not say whether the match was first suggested by an AI, so this counts all human-approved matches.

question: How many paintings are not open access?
sparql: SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?w) AS ?n) WHERE { ?w a mc:Work ; mc:dataset "paintings-1850-1900" . FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?w dcterms:license ?lic } }
explanation: Counts works in the 1850–1900 paintings collection that have no licence, which is how the graph marks a record that is not open access. Since no artist or collection was named, "paintings" is taken to mean that collection.

question: Which paintings are only attributed to, after, or imitating Vincent van Gogh?
explanation: Finds works whose link to Vincent van Gogh is only qualified (for example "attributed to", "after" or "imitator of"), showing the attribution label and the museum. It matches any qualified-artist record whose name contains "Van Gogh", because these attributions are often stored under their own labels such as "Imitator of Vincent van Gogh".

question: Portraits of women at the Met
explanation: This finds works at The Met that have a portrait subject and a subject about women or girls. It includes both museum-recorded and AI-suggested subjects, and covers both collections: the 1850–1900 paintings and the Rembrandt works.

question: Which Impressionist painters have works in more than one museum?
explanation: This finds artists whose Wikidata movement is Impressionism and lists those with works plainly attributed to them in at least two different museums. Works only 'after' or 'attributed to' them are not counted.
